ConnectionStrings.//: Supplied per environment. Locally this comes from .NET user secrets, written by scripts/db.ps1 or scripts/db.sh. Never commit a credential here.

Media.//: Mode is read literally: Disabled, Deterministic, or Real. It is never inferred from whether a credential is present, because a silent fall back to the in-memory store would look like a working upload and lose the master. Real requires AccountName, and the video provider additionally requires TokenId, TokenSecret, WebhookSecret, SigningKeyId, and SigningKeyBase64 — all from user secrets or key vault, never from this file.

Commerce.//: Same rule as Media: Mode is literal, never inferred from key presence. Real requires SecretKey and WebhookSecret from user secrets or Key Vault — never from this file.

EntraExternalId.//: Public identifiers only. There is no client secret: the API validates tokens and never calls the identity provider on its own behalf. Set Enabled=true and fill these in per environment (user secrets locally) to turn on real authentication.
